solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: How long it took God to create, say

definitions.text: How long it took God to create, say

parts.note: D is short for Deus, Latin for God

indicators.note: to create is to make something new, so the letters of the following word are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Bible-study question: how long did the creation take, as in the six of them?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: D for God, then 'create' rearranges SAY into AYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis measures the creation in units of time: six of them, with a seventh for rest.

clue.text: No more Post Office? Right time to deliver abroad

parts.note: ex- means former, no more

explanation.surface: A complaint that with the Post Office gone, it is the right moment to send goods overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship goods to a foreign market for sale is the trading sense of the word.

clue.text: Get comfortable with ET? Listen to alien

indicators.note: alien means strange or foreign, so the letters are made unfamiliar by reordering

explanation.surface: Advice for warming to the film's extraterrestrial: just hear the alien out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alien' looks like ET's own description but rearranges ETLISTENTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow accustomed to a new situation or place is a phrasal-verb synonym for becoming at ease there.

clue.text: Trite composition follows B sharp

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the letter B

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are assembled afresh

explanation.surface: A musical note: a hackneyed piece of music played after a B sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B sharp' looks like a musical note; B is wordplay and 'sharp' the definition. 'composition' turns TRITE into ITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp taste, acrid and biting, is a synonym for the tang of something like lemon peel.

clue.text: Put down a small plot, after felony was twice curtailed

indicators.note: the plot piece comes after the shortened crime
curtailed means tail cut off, done twice so the last two letters go

parts.note: a felony is a serious crime
a bed is a garden plot, as in a flower bed

explanation.surface: A legal note: someone puts down a small piece of land after a felony charge is reduced twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice curtailed' drops ME from CRIME to leave CRI.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something down to a cause, attributing it, is a synonym, as in putting a failure down to bad luck.

clue.text: Light from television system needs energy

parts.note: PAL is the analogue colour TV broadcasting standard used in Britain and Europe
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A technical note that a TV broadcasting system needs power to give out light.
explanation.definitionFit: A light colour is a faint, washed-out one, so the two adjectives are synonyms for shades.

clue.text: It's minute 'n' massless (or thereabouts)

indicators.note: thereabouts suggests the letters are only roughly in place, so they are reordered
M is the physics symbol for mass, so without mass removes that letter

explanation.surface: A description of a subatomic particle: tiny and with almost no mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'massless' takes M out of MINUTE N, and 'thereabouts' rearranges the remaining INUTEN with OR.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle is tiny and was long thought to have zero mass; it has only a minute one, so the clue describes it.

clue.text: Time to mock up original design

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to rib is to tease or mock

indicators.note: original means the first, so the opening letter of design is taken

explanation.surface: An artist decides it is time to sketch a mock-up of the first design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RIB into BIR. Time in British slang (from rhyming slang 'bird lime') is a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing time in prison is called doing this in British slang, from rhyming slang for time.

clue.text: One with sixteen wheels carrying international concerns

parts.note: one is a, the indefinite article

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other
to wheel is to turn round, so the letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: A lorry with sixteen wheels transporting cargo for an international firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' looks like part of the truck but rearranges SIXTEEN into NXETIES, and 'carrying' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Worries are concerns: both mean things that trouble the mind.

clue.text: Asian touring Zaire?

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: A question about whether an Asian traveller is on a tour of Zaire.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Azerbaijan, in the Caucasus, counts as Asian.

clue.text: Wide? Stumped! End of innings

parts.note: ST is the cricket scoring abbreviation for stumped
in cricket an innings ends when a batsman is out

explanation.surface: Cricket commentary: a wide ball, a stumping, and the innings is over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach, and stumped is a way of being dismissed; here 'Wide' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout means broad or fat in build, a synonym for wide in girth.

clue.text: Demonstrate freely, not as bothered

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so the letters are set loose and reordered
not means the following word is left out

explanation.surface: An invitation to protest freely, without being troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges DEMONSTRATE; 'not' then removes the letters A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tormented is distressed or harassed, so troubled and bothered are synonyms.

clue.text: Aardvark or elephant? Be a risky selection

indicators.note: a selection is a part picked out of the whole, so the answer is taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: Picking between an aardvark and an elephant could be a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an alternative name for the African aardvark, the burrowing ant-eating mammal.

clue.text: Top Cat pinches Dibble's seat in church

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip, so the piece holds another inside it
to top is to cut the head off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a tabby is a cat with a striped coat

indicators.note: a seat is a bottom, the end part of the word

explanation.surface: A cartoon caper: Top Cat steals Officer Dibble's place in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Cat is a cartoon alley cat always outwitting Officer Dibble. Here 'Top' says behead TABBY to ABBY, which takes E, the last letter of Dibble, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastic church, such as Westminster's, is called by this name.

clue.text: European shake up enabling Norway to leave

indicators.note: shaking something up disturbs its order, so these letters are rearranged
to leave means a letter departs from the word

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A political shake-up in Europe that lets Norway quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shake up' rearranges ENABLING; 'to leave' then takes one N away.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Belgium is an example of a European.

clue.text: Bad luck splitting rent rates below student flat

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts the following pieces under the first

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, standing for student

indicators.note: splitting means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other
rent here means torn apart, so the letters are scattered
bad suggests the letters are spoilt and so jumbled

explanation.surface: A grumble about student housing: bad luck as rents and rates fall below a student flat's worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' and 'rates' read as housing costs, but 'rent' means torn and signals a rearrangement; 'Bad' does the same job, and 'splitting' sends one jumble into the other, beneath the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and lifeless, without sparkle: a flat performance is a synonym.

clue.text: Bottom of storm drain

indicators.note: to storm is to rage, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: The bottom of a storm drain, where water collects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm drain' looks like a single item; 'storm' is the signal for rearranging DRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point, astronomically or figuratively, is a synonym for rock bottom.

clue.text: Former PM Blair abandoning the centre, now criminal

indicators.note: losing its middle leaves only the outside letters of Blair
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A political accusation that Tony Blair has deserted the centre ground and is now a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning the centre' keeps B and R, and 'criminal' rearranges NOW into OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon, Blair's successor, was the British Prime Minister from 2007 to 2010.

clue.text: Locations of birds or eels, 50% with snakes

indicators.note: to snake is to wind about, so the letters twist into a new order
half of the word, here its first two letters

explanation.surface: A zoo directory listing birds, eels and half the reptiles house snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' takes WI from 'with'; 'snakes' looks like reptiles but rearranges OREELS plus WI.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where owls nest or are kept: the -ery suffix names a home for creatures, like a rookery.

clue.text: Early or later?

definitions.meaning: early means from long ago, as in earlier times
later in life, aged, as in later years

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions look like opposites; one means of former times, the other of advanced age.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient times and advanced years both use this adjective: the olden days, and the elderly.

clue.text: Fish in batter to be past its sell-by date

indicators.note: in means the fish goes inside the other letters
to batter is to beat, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A chip-shop warning: fish in batter that has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like fish-and-chips coating but rearranges TO BE into OBTE, and 'in' puts SOLE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of date and no longer in use, like goods past their expiry, is a synonym.

clue.text: Sound, sound material

indicators.note: the second sound tells us the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: corduroy is a ribbed cloth, often shortened to cord

explanation.walkthrough: The repeat is the trick: one 'sound' is the definition, the other is the signal for a word said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Several musical notes played together make a single harmonious sound.

clue.text: Field swirls with blues and other colours

indicators.note: to swirl is to turn round, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a ley is a field of pasture
lows are low moods, the blues

explanation.surface: A painter's meadow, with whirls of blue among other hues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirls' turns LEY into YEL. 'other colours' is fair because blues are colours too.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades like lemon and gold are colours distinct from the blues in the surface.

clue.text: At first, Pompeii's lava flowed about, circling commotion

indicators.note: the opening letter of Pompeii is taken
lava that has flowed has moved, so its letters change places
circling means going round, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A scene from Vesuvius: molten lava flowing round Pompeii amid the chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowed' rearranges LAVA into ALAV, and 'circling' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss and bother, much ado about nothing, is a synonym for a commotion.

clue.text: He carries Philip or Terry inside

indicators.note: inside means the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: A man carrying Philip or Terry indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A luggage carrier at a hotel or station is someone whose job is to bear loads.

clue.text: European city where 6 queen was raised

parts.note: six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: Anne was a Queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: A royal biography: the city where six queens were brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is just the number in Roman numerals. 'was raised' turns ANNE into ENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Austria is a major city in Europe.

clue.text: It clambers off road to begin with?

definitions.text: It clambers off road to begin with?

indicators.note: off means not right, so the letters are disordered
the first letter of road is taken

explanation.surface: A riddle about a motorbike that goes off-road over rough ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CLAMBERS plus R. The whole clue describes an off-road motorcycle and also someone scrambling up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcycle built for rough off-road racing, and anyone who climbs on all fours, both fit the description.

clue.text: Plants and animals?

definitions.meaning: plants means scatters seed in the ground
female pigs, an example of animals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plants' looks like a noun, as in flora, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb for planting seed and the noun for female pigs are spelt the same.

clue.text: Maybe algebra, trigonometry, histograms, primes for Americans?

definitions.text: Maybe algebra, trigonometry, histograms, primes for Americans?

indicators.note: primes are firsts, so the opening letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: A list of school maths topics, as Americans would call the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primes' looks like another maths topic in the list, but it signals the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra and trigonometry are branches of what the US calls the subject the British call maths.

clue.text: Half of Amsterdam's compounds go with speed

indicators.note: to compound is to mix together, so the letters are combined in a new order
the first half of the word, five of its nine letters

explanation.surface: A chemistry-and-drugs picture: half of Amsterdam's substances work with speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compounds' and 'speed' suggest drugs; 'compounds' rearranges AMSTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To move fast, as a train under full pressure does, is an idiom: to steam ahead.

clue.text: Fashion icon's very upset to wear two dress sizes

indicators.note: to wear is to have on, so the sizes go around the other letters

parts.note: M is the clothing size medium
S is the clothing size small

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A supermodel so distraught that she must squeeze into two dress sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two dress sizes' supplies two separate letters, medium and small, which 'to wear' wraps round the overturned 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate, the British supermodel, is a celebrated name in the fashion world.

clue.text: Sorry to cover earth with grass

indicators.note: to cover means to go over, so the first word encloses the letter

parts.note: Sorry? and What? are both ways of asking someone to repeat

explanation.surface: An apology for covering soil with turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' is not an apology but the question asked by someone who missed what was said.
explanation.definitionFit: This cereal crop is botanically a member of the grass family.

clue.text: As reported in Dublin, 300 signs of growth

indicators.note: in an Irish accent the th sound is said as a plain t, so the words are heard as an Irish speaker says them

parts.note: the figure is a 3 followed by zeros, which look like rings

explanation.surface: A news item from Dublin about growth figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 300 written out shows a 3 followed by circles; an Irish accent drops the h from three.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual bands seen in a cut trunk show how many years the trunk has grown.
